rooms.14676: An immense oak stands here, so old that its heart has rotted clean away, leaving a hollow trunk wide enough for three people to shelter inside. The deep gully that has run beside the path peters out here into a shallow dell of ferns and dead leaves. North, a narrow path climbs along the gully's rim, while the forest runs on east and south beneath a canopy so thick that the light comes down green. Acorn cups crunch underfoot, and the air smells of damp bark.
rooms.14674: The path keeps close to the lip of a steep gully here, with only a fringe of ivy between your boots and the drop. A tall ash leans out over the gap at a perilous angle, half its roots torn bare and clutching at empty air. Mist lies thick in the bottom of the gully, hiding the floor of rotting leaves far below. The rim path runs north and south, and the trees stand a little more open to the east.
rooms.14636: A narrow strip of level ground runs between the edge of the gully and the trunks of the forest, worn into a path by the hooves of passing deer. Holly bushes crowd the rim, their glossy leaves pricking at your sleeves, and the drop beyond them is lost in shadow. A moss-furred log lies beside the path like a bench left out for travellers. The way runs north toward the beech wood and south along the gully, while the forest opens east beneath tall oaks.
rooms.14626: Here the beech wood ends at the head of a deep gully that curves away out of sight, its sides steep with loose earth and dangling roots. A path follows the rim south, squeezed between the drop and a row of young beeches. North and west, smooth grey trunks stand in orderly ranks above a carpet of copper leaves, and the forest continues east. From somewhere down in the gully comes the slow drip of water onto stone.
rooms.14614: The beeches here are tall and as smooth as cast pewter, bare of branches until high overhead, where their leaves knit into a pale green roof. Almost nothing grows beneath them, and the ground is a dry, rustling carpet of copper leaves and split beech-mast. Someone long ago carved letters into the bark of the nearest trunk, and the growing tree has swollen them into broad, scarred shapes. Daylight brightens to the north toward the edge of the forest.
rooms.14602: The forest thins toward its northern edge here, and daylight pours between the trunks to wake a thicket of bramble and young birch. Beyond the last trees to the north, the open sky shows as bright as a window. A deer path wriggles through the brambles toward the eaves, while the beech wood darkens again to the south and runs on east. The air is warmer, and it carries the smell of sun-dried grass from the country outside.
rooms.14601: A row of ancient pollarded oaks stands here, each cut back at head height long ago, so that its squat trunk swells into a great knuckled head bristling with a crown of branches. The glade between them is grassy and bright, sprinkled with the small yellow stars of tormentil. The open country lies just beyond the trees to the north. Paths wander east and west along the inside of the eaves, and the beech wood rises tall to the south.
rooms.14613: In the heart of the beech wood the roots of four great trees meet around a hollow, where rainwater has gathered into a dark, still pool scattered with floating leaves. Pale fungi grow in tiers on a dead branch beside it, like rows of little shelves. The ground is clear of brush on every side, so you can see a long way between the grey trunks. A sunlit glade shows through the trees to the north.
rooms.14625: The beech wood stops short at the brink of a gully that cuts across the forest floor, steep-sided and choked at the bottom with years of dead leaves. Roots hang out over the edge like frayed ropes where the earth has crumbled away beneath them. There is no way across, but the rim leads on east and west beneath the beeches, and the wood rises gently to the north. A cold breath of air rises from the gully, smelling of rot and wet stone.
rooms.14624: An old oak grows at the very lip of the gully here, its crown dead and bare so that its topmost branches stand out above the leaves like a stag's antlers. Holly fills the gaps between the trunks, dark and glossy and armed with spines. Below the rim the gully drops away too steeply to climb, its far side a shadowy bank of ferns. The beech wood lies north, and the forest runs on east and west along the edge.
rooms.14612: A boulder as big as a cottage sits among the trees here, split clean in two as if by an axe, and a young rowan has rooted in the crack between the halves. Moss covers its top like a green fleece, and ferns trail from every ledge. Beech and oak grow together around it, and the ground slopes gently south toward a hidden gully. Brighter light shows to the north, where the forest nears its edge.
rooms.14600: Old hazel stools crowd this corner of the forest, each sprouting a dozen straight grey poles where some woodcutter coppiced them long ago and never came back. Bramble scrambles between them, and the light falls bright and broken through their leaves. The eaves of the forest lie only a few steps to the north. The way continues west into older trees, while a beech wood begins to the east and south.
rooms.14803: An old earthen bank runs along the edge of the forest here, topped with a row of gnarled hawthorns, as if someone once meant to keep the trees from spreading. On one side the wood stands dark and close; on the other, rough pasture rolls away under a wide sky toward distant grasslands. The bank leads east and west along the eaves, and a gap in it lets a path slip south into the bracken beneath the trees. The wind combs the long grass into silver waves.
rooms.14502: Bracken grows waist-high just inside the eaves, a sea of green fronds that hides the ground and rustles at every step. The trees are tall and widely spaced, mostly oak and birch, and the sky shows bright through the gaps to the north, where the forest ends. Faint trails part the bracken east and west, and the ferns run on south into deeper shade. A sweet, dusty smell rises from the fronds wherever they are brushed.
rooms.14505: The stump of an enormous tree rises from the ferns here, cut flat long ago and now crusted with grey and orange lichens. Its rings are far too many to count, and the axe marks around its edge have softened into shallow grooves. Lady ferns crowd about its base, their lacy fronds pale green in the shade. A deer track runs north and south past the stump, and the wood stretches away east and west.
rooms.14508: The ground dips here toward a mossy bank where hart's-tongue ferns grow in glossy, strap-shaped clumps. From just to the west comes the cool trickle of running water, and the air is noticeably damper. Ferns of a dozen kinds fill the spaces between slim ash trees, their tips dripping after the least shower. The forest continues north and south, and grows darker and older to the east.
rooms.14511: A fallen birch lies across the ferns here, its white bark peeling in papery curls and its wood gone soft as cheese. Bracket fungi have sprouted along its length in neat rows, like steps up the trunk. Through the ferns to the west you can hear a brook chattering over stones. The ground is soft and springy underfoot, and the way runs north and south between slender trees, with deeper forest to the east.
rooms.14514: Mounds of sandy earth spill from a row of holes dug beneath the roots of a towering ash, where badgers have tunnelled their sett for generations. Their paths are worn bare through the ferns, and a fallen branch nearby is scored with claw marks. The brook murmurs close by to the west. The forest runs on north and south through tall fronds, and eastward into deeper shade.
rooms.14519: The ferns thin out here around a small, round pond that fills the pit where some great tree was torn up by its roots long ago. Marsh marigolds blaze yellow along its edges, and its still surface holds a perfect picture of the leaves above. Old oaks lean in around the clearing as if to admire themselves. The ferns lie north, the brook runs close by to the west, and the wood grows older and mossier to the south and east.
rooms.14524: Boulders lie scattered among the oaks here, each so thickly cushioned with moss that its shape has softened into a smooth green hump. Moss climbs the trunks as well, and hangs in pale beards from the lower branches. The voice of the brook carries from the west, where it bends away toward the edge of the forest. Ferns lie north, and the mossy wood goes on south and east in deep, green quiet.
rooms.14527: A giant oak has fallen here, and its trunk lies across the forest floor higher than your head, furred with moss and sprouting a row of seedlings along its spine. Its torn roots rear up in a great disc of earth on one side, while its broken crown sprawls among the trees to the west. A gap where its branches snapped lets you pass north and south. The air under the canopy is still and heavy, and every sound seems to sink into the moss.
rooms.14530: An ancient ash has split near its base into three great trunks, each as thick as an ordinary tree, that rise and lean apart like the prongs of a fork. Deep moss covers the ground so evenly that your feet sink in without a sound, and here and there it is pressed into hollows where deer have bedded down. Ivy wraps the lower trunks in dark green coils. The mossy forest stretches away on every side, as quiet as a shut room.
rooms.14533: An old dry-stone wall crosses the forest here, so ancient and so swallowed by moss that it looks more like a long green bank than anything built by hands. Trees have grown up through it, and their roots have shouldered whole stretches down into heaps of stones. A gap lets the way pass south, and the wall runs on west through the trees. To the north the moss-hung oaks stand close and silent.
rooms.14536: Wild garlic carpets the ground here between tall, straight ash trees, its broad leaves and starry white flowers filling the air with a sharp green smell. The old mossy wall lies just to the north, broken down where the way passes through it. The forest floor dips gently toward the south. The canopy is high and light, and the ash leaves flutter at the faintest breath of wind.
rooms.14539: Grey rock shows through the trees to the east, where the ground rises toward the foot of a long scarp of crags. Boulders that tumbled from it long ago lie half buried in the forest floor, green with moss and fern. Ash and wych elm grow here, their leaves pale against the stone. The forest runs on north and south, and the moss-hung trees grow thicker to the west.
rooms.14577: The forest floor ends here against the first rise of a grey scarp, a wall of weathered rock that climbs higher and higher as it runs south. Ivy and polypody ferns cling to its ledges, and its foot is littered with mossy stones. The way follows the base of the rock south, while the forest continues north and opens west among ash and elm. Water seeps from a crack in the stone, darkening it in a long stripe.
rooms.14578: The scarp rises to twice a man's height here, its face broken into massive square blocks like the steps of a stair built for giants, though none of them could be climbed. A yew has taken root at its foot and grown sideways along the rock, twisted into knots by its long struggle for light. The path runs north and south beneath the stone, and the forest lies west. It is cool here, and the air smells of wet rock and yew needles.
rooms.14579: The scarp leans outward above the path here, forming a shallow overhang where travellers have long sheltered from the rain. Its ceiling is blackened with the soot of countless small fires, and a ring of fire-cracked stones sits on the dry earth beneath it. Beyond its shelter the forest drips and rustles. The way runs north and south along the foot of the rock, and the trees open to the west.
rooms.14580: A rockfall has spilled from the scarp here, burying its foot under a jumble of angular boulders, some as big as wagons. Moss and fern have softened the heap, but the gaps between the stones are deep and dark, and you must pick your way with care. The path winds through the jumble north and south, and the forest is easier going to the west. A few stunted birches have rooted among the stones.
rooms.14581: High on the face of the scarp, a rowan grows straight out of a crack, its berries hanging scarlet over the drop. Below it the ledges are streaked white where owls have roosted for years, and the ground at the foot of the rock is scattered with grey pellets of fur and tiny bones. The path keeps to the base of the cliff, running north and south. The forest to the west is dim and close.
rooms.14582: A thin thread of water falls from the top of the scarp here, unravelling into spray long before it reaches the stony pool at its foot. The rock behind it is slick and green, and the ferns around the pool shiver in the cool draught the falling water makes. Stepping stones carry the path across the pool's overflow, north and south along the cliff. The forest lies west, dim and dripping.
rooms.14583: The face of the scarp has been worn smooth here by the weather, and someone in ages past chose it for carving. Spirals and branching lines run across the stone, along with the unmistakable outline of a great antlered stag, all softened by moss creeping in from the edges. The ground before the carvings is bare and trodden. The path continues north and south under the rock, and the wood stretches away west.
rooms.14584: A deep fissure splits the scarp from top to bottom here, far too narrow for anyone to squeeze into. Cold air breathes steadily out of it, carrying a smell of wet stone and the faint, far-off sound of dripping somewhere inside the rock. Hart's-tongue ferns grow thickly around its mouth, fed by the damp. The path runs north and south along the cliff, and the forest opens to the west.
rooms.14585: The scarp is lower here, and dark yews cling along its top, their roots pouring over the edge in a knotted cascade. Beneath them the path is carpeted with fallen red needles and the hard husks of yew berries. Mist creeps in among the trees from the low, damp wood to the west. North the cliff climbs steadily higher, and south it bends sharply away.
rooms.14586: Here the scarp bends at a sharp angle and runs off east, its face lower and more broken, with a twisted hawthorn growing in the very corner of the rock. A path follows its foot that way beneath beeches, while the taller cliffs climb away north. The trees thin a little to the south, where the forest's edge is near, and a misty, low-lying wood spreads to the west.
rooms.14590: Beeches grow hard against the foot of a low rock wall here, and their roots have gripped the stone like the fingers of giants, flowing over it in smooth grey coils and prising it apart. The ground between them is a lattice of more roots, and you must step high to cross it. The way runs east and west along the base of the rock, and the trees open southward toward the edge of the forest.
rooms.14588: The rock wall dwindles here into a steep bank of earth and stones, held together by a mesh of roots. A storm once tore through this part of the forest, and fallen trunks lie at all angles, some still caught leaning in the arms of their neighbours. Brambles and young birches have sprung up in the light the storm let in. Paths pick their way through the wreckage east, west and south.
rooms.14589: This is the heart of the storm's damage, where whole ranks of trees were thrown down together, and their great discs of roots now stand on edge, taller than a house. Rainwater fills the craters they tore from the ground, black and still. The sky is open overhead, and willowherb and bramble have claimed the light. A way leads east toward a cleft in the rocky ridge, and others wind west and south among the fallen trunks.
rooms.14598: The low, rocky ridge that walls this part of the forest is cut through here by a narrow ravine, which opens northward between walls of fern-hung stone. A trickle of water runs out of it over a bed of pale pebbles and sinks into the ground before it has gone ten paces. Storm-felled trees lie to the west, and tall beeches stand east and south. The air flowing out of the ravine is cool and smells of moss.
rooms.14597: A wall of grey rock rises sheer on one side of the way, dripping with water and hung with ferns, while on the other the ground climbs gently into the forest to the east. The bed of the ravine is stony and damp, and a trickle threads between the stones toward its mouth to the south. Northward the walls draw closer together. Moss grows so thick on the rock that it would hold the print of a hand.
rooms.14596: The ravine deepens here, and its rock wall towers overhead, streaked with dark seepage and tufted with ferns in every crack. On the opposite side a steep slope of roots and earth climbs up into the forest to the east. Fallen leaves have drifted deep in the ravine's bed and rustle around your ankles. The way narrows to the north and widens toward the ravine's mouth to the south.
rooms.14591: Rock walls close in on both sides until the ravine is barely wider than a cart, and the sky is only a ragged strip of green and light far above. Every footstep comes back twice from the stone. Water drips from overhanging ledges, and the floor is a bed of wet moss and stones. The ravine ends a little way to the north, and widens again as it runs south.
rooms.14592: The ravine ends here in a tall wall of rock that weeps water from a hundred cracks, so that its whole face glistens and drips. At its foot the water has gathered into a round, clear pool lined with green stones, cold enough to numb the hand. A rowan leans from a ledge above it, and the walls on every side are far too steep and slick to climb. The only way out is back south along the ravine.
rooms.14748: A lightning-struck oak stands at the centre of a small glade here, its trunk split from crown to root and scorched black along the wound, though green leaves still sprout from one half. Harebells and bracken crowd the sunny ground around it. The way west leads toward the mouth of a rocky ravine, while the forest runs north, east and south beneath tall beeches. A faint smell of old burning still clings to the riven wood.
rooms.14749: A dense thicket of holly closes in here, dark and glossy and impossible to push through, so that the way must bend around it. The ground beneath the hollies is bare and brown, littered with dead spiny leaves that crackle and prick. Tall beeches stand to the east and west of the thicket, and the trees thin to the south toward the edge of the forest. The air is cool and very still.
rooms.14732: Beeches and hornbeams share this part of the forest, their grey trunks twisted like knotted muscle. Between the spreading roots of the largest beech, something has scraped out a deep den, ringed with heaps of broken branches, torn moss and shed feathers as long as your forearm. The earth around it is churned and smells rank. The forest stretches north and east, a holly thicket lies to the west, and the trees thin southward toward the eaves.
rooms.14731: Daylight floods in from the south, where the forest ends a few steps away and open hillside begins. Bracken and gorse have crept in under the outer trees, and the wind that reaches this far smells of heather and sun-warmed stone. A rotting line of fence posts marks where someone once tried to keep the hill's sheep from straying into the woods. Tall grey beeches rise to the north, and the forest runs on east and west.
rooms.14846: Outside the forest's edge the land climbs into rough hill pasture, cropped short and scattered with grey stones, toward a line of hazy blue mountains far beyond. A dry-stone wall, half fallen, follows the eaves here as if to fence the forest in. The trees stand tall to the north, and a sheep track runs east and west along the wall. The wind blows steadily off the hills, cool and clean.
rooms.14847: A squat stone kiln stands just outside the eaves, its round walls half fallen and its arched mouth still black with old burning. Pale, chalky stones lie heaped around it, and nettles grow thick where the lime once spilled. Beyond it the hillside rises bare toward the distant peaks. A track runs east and west along the edge of the forest, and the trees lie close to the north.
rooms.14751: Grey stones break through the thin soil here, and the beeches that grow among them have spread their roots wide across the rock in search of earth. One flat stone has a round hollow worn into its top, brimming with rainwater. Light comes in from the south, where the trees end, and a holly thicket darkens the way to the north. The going is easier east and west along the slope.
rooms.14750: A spring rises among the beeches here, bubbling up through a ring of white sand in a basin no bigger than a cartwheel, so clear that every grain can be seen dancing. Watercress and brooklime choke the little runnel that drains it away into the leaves. The light is brighter to the south, where the forest ends. Paths lead north toward a sunny glade, and east and west through the trees.
rooms.14848: A lone hawthorn grows on the open slope outside the eaves, bent almost double by the wind and hung with tufts of wool snagged from passing flocks. The hillside beyond climbs in long, stony swells toward far blue mountains. The forest stands close to the north, its edge running east and west along the foot of the slope. The grass here is short and springy and starred with tiny yellow flowers.
rooms.14849: Water seeps out of the hillside here and soaks the ground just outside the eaves, so that rushes and tufts of cotton grass grow in soggy patches. Stepping from tussock to tussock keeps your boots mostly dry. The forest's edge runs east and west, with the trees rising tall to the north, while the hills climb away bare and grey beyond the wet ground. A cold breeze comes down off the slopes.
rooms.14599: A dry bed of pale pebbles winds between the trees here, marking the course that water from the ravine to the north must take in wetter seasons. Birch and beech grow along its banks, and the light is clear and bright from the open hills to the south. Storm-felled trunks lie in a tangle to the west. Eastward, the beeches gather around a spring that boils up through white sand.
rooms.14595: The remains of an old sunken track run south out of the forest here, its banks lined with roots and its bed choked with fern and bramble. Few feet have used it in years. To the north, fallen trees lie in a tangle where a storm once flattened the wood, and the forest runs on east and west among younger growth. A squat marker stone stands beside the track, its letters long since worn away.
rooms.14850: An old road climbs out of the forest here and heads south into the hills toward the distant Great Valley, but a heavy gate of grey timbers bars it between two stone posts, chained and locked with rust. Beyond the gate the road vanishes under thorn and landslip. The eaves of the forest run east and west, and a sunken track leads back north beneath the trees. The wind whistles thinly through the gaps in the gate.
rooms.14851: A great cairn of grey stones crowns a knoll outside the forest here, built higher than a man and capped with a flat slab. From beside it you can look out over the endless green roof of the forest, and on a clear day catch a far grey glint of the sea. The forest's edge runs east and west at the foot of the knoll, and the trees rise close to the north. Lichen grows in pale rings on the stones.
rooms.14594: Fallen trees from an old storm lie thick here, and the way passes beneath one great beech that came down across two others, forming a low, dark arch of grey bark. Young birches crowd the gaps in a pale thicket, and brambles snatch at your legs. To the south the forest ends and the light grows brighter. Ways lead north into the worst of the wreckage, and east and west through the trees.
rooms.14593: An enormous beech stands here on roots that arch above the ground like the buttresses of a temple, and between two of them someone has woven a low shelter of hazel sticks, long abandoned and grown through with ivy. The forest floor is a tangle of smaller roots and beech-mast. The light is brighter to the south, where the forest ends, and the trees continue north, east and west.
rooms.14852: A roofless stone bothy stands just outside the eaves, where some shepherd once sheltered with his flock. Its walls are still sound to shoulder height and a soot-stained hearth fills one end, but the roof timbers fell in long ago. Beyond it the hills climb away, stony and bare. The edge of the forest runs east and west, and the trees rise tall to the north.
rooms.14853: A tall boundary stone stands in the rough grass outside the eaves, leaning a little and splotched with yellow lichen. Its two broad faces are carved, one with a spreading tree and the other with a mountain peak, as if to mark where the forest's country ends and the hills begin. The eaves run east and west, and the forest rises to the north, where a ragged crag shows among the trees. Thistles grow thick around the stone's foot.
rooms.14587: A last outlying crag of the scarp stands here, no higher than a cottage roof, so thickly clothed in ivy that it looks like a green mound with a stunted oak on top. The forest's edge lies just to the south, and wind from the hills stirs the leaves. A path runs north toward the corner of the cliffs, and others lead east among great beeches and west into a quiet, misty wood.
rooms.14570: Mist drifts between slender alders here, thinning toward the south, where the trees end and pale daylight shows. A little burn comes in from the hills that way and loses itself in the soft ground, spreading into brown pools between tussocks of sedge. An ivy-covered crag rises among the trees to the east. The wood runs north into deeper mist and west along the inside of the eaves.
rooms.14567: Old grey willows sprawl across the ground here, their trunks lying flat where they fell and sending up new shoots like rows of green spears. Pools of standing water reflect the pale mist that hangs among them. The foot of a rocky scarp shows through the trees to the east. The way north and south keeps to firmer ground between the pools, and the misty wood spreads west.
rooms.14564: Webs as wide as cartwheels are strung between the yews here, beaded with mist so that every thread hangs heavy with silver drops. The dry husks of moths and beetles dangle in them like strange fruit. The ground is dark with fallen needles, and the scarp rises close by to the east. The way runs north and south, and the mist grows thicker to the west.
rooms.14561: Reeds and tall sedges rise around you here at the edge of a dark mere, whose still water shows through the mist to the west. The ground quakes faintly underfoot, a crust of moss and roots over deep mud, and the air smells of rot and peat. Firmer ground leads north and south along the shore, and the rocky scarp lies east beyond a screen of alders.
rooms.14558: Bog myrtle grows thickly on the wet ground here, and every brush against its leaves releases a sharp, sweet, resinous smell. Through the mist to the west lies the dark water of a mere, rimmed with reeds. Pale fingers of vapour curl up from the ground and drift between the birches. The way north and south follows a ridge of drier earth, and the carved face of the scarp shows faintly to the east.
rooms.14555: The sound of falling water comes through the trees from the east, where a thin cascade drops from the top of the scarp. Alders grow here in wet ground, their roots raised in arches above black pools, and moss hangs from every branch. The mist thickens to the south toward a hidden mere. The way north leads onto higher, drier ground, and a path of split logs begins to the west.
rooms.14552: The ground rises a little here into a hummock of firm earth where three old oaks grow close together, their roots locked in a single tangle. Mist pools in the hollows on every side, and the lower branches drip steadily. Through the trees to the east, the scarp shows grey and streaked with white where owls have long roosted on its ledges. The way runs north and south, and west deeper into the misty wood.
rooms.14549: A boulder that rolled from the scarp long ago lies here among the trees, and a birch has grown right over it, its roots draped down every side of the stone like a net. Mist hangs low beneath the canopy. The jumble of the rockfall lies to the east at the foot of the cliffs. The way leads north and south through the damp wood, and west toward the forest's misty heart.
rooms.14546: Here the mossy wood begins to slope gently downward, and the first wisps of mist creep up through the trees from the low, wet ground to the south. Old ash trees stand well apart, their trunks green with moss on one side only. To the east the scarp leans out over a shallow rock shelter. The forest runs north among older trees and west into growing dimness.
rooms.14542: A single shaft of sunlight falls through a gap in the canopy here, lighting a mossy stump so brightly that it seems to glow against the shadows. Around it the forest is old and hushed, its floor deep in moss and the brown skeletons of last year's leaves. The great stepped blocks of the scarp rise through the trees to the east. Ways lead north and south between the trunks, and west into the moss-hung wood.
rooms.14541: Low lines of mossy stones mark out the foundations of a small building here, a forester's lodge perhaps, long since fallen and forgotten. A broad hearthstone still lies at one end, cracked across, with a holly growing up through the crack. Of the chimney nothing remains but a tumbled heap. The forest closes round on every side, and paths lead off north and south among the oaks.
rooms.14538: Bluebells carpet the ground under the oaks here, so thickly that the forest floor seems wreathed in a haze of blue smoke. Their scent is faint and sweet in the still air. The oaks are huge and ancient, their lower limbs as thick as ordinary trees and furred with moss. The way runs north toward a great yew, and the wood continues south, east and west.
rooms.14535: An enormous yew grows here, so old that its trunk has split and hollowed into a ring of separate pillars, and you could walk right into the dark space at its heart. Its branches sweep down to the ground all round, making a dim, red-brown chamber of needles and bark. The old mossy wall runs close by to the north. Beyond the yew's shade, the forest continues south, east and west.
rooms.14532: Two tall gateposts of grey stone still stand in the old mossy wall here, though the gate that once hung between them rotted away an age ago. One post bears a carving half hidden beneath the moss. The wall runs away east and west through the trees, broken and green, and the gap between the posts leads south. North, the forest is deep and silent around a ring of standing stones.
rooms.14529: Nine stones stand in a ring among the trees here, none taller than a man's shoulder, each so thick with moss that they look like hooded figures gathered in council. No tree grows inside the ring, though the forest crowds right up to its edge, and the moss within is short and fine as a lawn. The air is utterly still. The way runs north and south past the circle, and the forest stretches east and west.
rooms.14526: The broken crown of a fallen giant oak fills this part of the forest, a tangle of great limbs, snapped branches and dead leaves that you must clamber around. Its mossy trunk stretches away to the east, as long as a barn. Ferns and seedlings have begun to claim the wreckage. The brook can be heard to the north, and the way south leads toward a ring of standing stones.
rooms.14523: The brook that runs down from the north swings sharply west here, scouring a deep pool at the bend where the water turns slowly, dark and clear. A bar of pale gravel has built up on the inside of the curve. Royal ferns stand tall on the banks, and the boulders around are thick with moss. The forest continues east and south, and the brook leads away west toward the edge of the trees.
rooms.14518: A clear brook runs south here over a bed of brown pebbles, and a line of flat stepping stones crosses it, each one worn smooth and dished in the middle. Watercress grows in the slack water by the banks. On one side the ferns are tall and thick, and on the other a lawn of moss leads east toward a round pond. The brook can be followed north toward its source.
rooms.14513: The brook drops over a ledge of dark rock here in a small, noisy fall no higher than your knee, and churns into a pool of foam before running on south. Ferns lean over the water from both banks, their fronds beaded with spray. A badger path crosses the brook just below the fall. The ferns go on north and west, and the forest grows older to the east.
rooms.14510: Still young here, the brook is narrow enough to step across, and it runs south between undercut banks where tree roots dangle into the water like pale threads. The ground on either side is spongy with moss and fern. Its source, a spring, rises just to the north. To the east a fallen birch lies across the ferns, and the forest runs on west toward the light at its edge.
rooms.14507: Here a spring wells up from beneath a moss-covered boulder into a round stone basin, and spills over its lip to begin a brook that runs away south. The basin looks too regular to be natural, as if hands shaped it long ago. Ferns crowd every side, glistening in the damp air. The water is ice-cold and tastes faintly of stone, and paths lead north, east and west through the ferns.
rooms.14504: A muddy wallow lies in a dip among the ferns here, churned by cloven hooves and rimmed with tufts of russet hair snagged on the brambles where red deer come to roll and cool themselves. The earth around it smells rank and sour. The ferns are shoulder-high and heavy with dew. The way north leads toward the edge of the forest, and from the south comes the soft trickle of a spring.
rooms.14501: A weathered wooden post stands among the bracken just inside the eaves, its arms long broken off and only peg holes left to show that it was ever a signpost. Birches grow here, their white trunks bright against the darker forest to the south. The open country is very close to the north, and the wind reaches in to stir the ferns. Trails lead east and west along the inside of the eaves.
rooms.14802: The ground swells into a gorse-covered rise just outside the forest, the spiny bushes bright with yellow flowers that smell warm and sweet in the sun. From the top you can see far out over rolling country, where the land opens into wide grasslands under an enormous sky. The forest stands at your back to the south, dark and tall. The eaves run east and west, edged by an old earthen bank.
rooms.14801: A sandy track runs along the outside of the eaves here, rutted by long-gone carts and scraped by rabbits. Grass gives way to heather and gorse toward the forest's corner to the west, and the wind carries a faint tang of salt. The trees stand close to the south, a mix of birch and oak bent by the weather. The track leads on east along the edge of the forest.
rooms.14500: Light comes in from two sides at once in this corner of the forest, for the eaves lie only a few steps to the north and to the west. The trees here are stunted and bent by the wind, their crowns all leaning the same way, and bracken grows lush in the brightness beneath them. A salt smell drifts in from the open heath. The forest deepens to the south and east.
rooms.14503: Heather has crept in under the trees from the heath outside, mingling with the bracken in a tangle of purple and green. The trees here are birch and rowan, light and airy, and the brightness of the open land shows between them to the west. A path leads east into taller ferns, and the edge of the forest runs north and south. The wind sets the birch leaves trembling.
rooms.14506: A wind-thrown pine lies here with its shallow roots in the air, a rare dark conifer among the birches, and its fallen needles have turned the ground beneath it a rusty brown. The land slopes gently east toward a spring hidden in the ferns. Daylight from the open heath brightens the trees to the west. The way north and south keeps along the inside of the forest's edge.
rooms.14509: A long, straight-sided pit lies among the ferns here, an old woodcutters' sawpit where one man once stood below and one above to rip logs into planks. It is half full of leaves now, and ferns sprout from its walls. Hawthorns bent by the sea wind line the edge of the forest to the west. The brook runs close by to the east, and the way leads north and south.
rooms.14512: Low, broad oaks grow here near the edge of the forest, their branches swept all one way by years of wind from the sea, and grey-green lichen hangs from them in long beards. The ground is a mix of moss and short ferns. The brook can be heard splashing over a little fall to the east. The heath lies just beyond the trees to the west, and the forest runs on north and south.
rooms.14517: A grove of old hollies grows here, so dense overhead that the ground beneath is dry and bare even after rain. Their trunks are smooth and pale, and the shade under them is deep and still, sheltered from the wind off the heath. Outside the grove, ferns crowd up to the edge of the forest to the west. Stepping stones cross the brook a little way east, and the way runs north and south.
rooms.14522: The brook flows west here toward the forest's edge, broadening into a shallow ford over pale sand where the water ripples ankle-deep. Alders lean over it, their roots knotted along the banks. Through the thinning trees to the west, the stream runs out onto the open heath. Upstream the brook bends away east toward a deep pool, and the forest runs on north and south.
rooms.14525: Honeysuckle twines up the trunks of young oaks near the edge of the forest here, and its scent hangs heavy and sweet in the shelter of the trees. Dog roses scramble through the undergrowth, catching at sleeves. Light from the heath brightens the way to the west. Eastward lies the broken crown of a fallen giant, and the forest runs on north toward the brook and south into mossier ground.
rooms.14528: Cushion moss has grown into great soft mounds between the trees here, some as high as your knee, in every shade of green from almost yellow to almost black. Rotting stumps stand among them, shelved with bracket fungi as broad as plates. A strange stillness hangs over the wood to the east, where a ring of stones stands among the trees. The edge of the forest lies west, and the way runs north and south.
rooms.14531: The old mossy wall that crosses the forest comes to an end here, running out from under the trees to the west and fading into a line of grassy stones on the heath beyond. Its last stretch is little more than a hump of moss with a few stones showing through. The wall leads away east toward a pair of standing gateposts. The forest continues north, and south the ground begins to fall gently away.
rooms.14534: Through a gap in the trees to the west, a tall standing stone can be seen leaning on the open heath just outside the forest. Inside the eaves the ground is a mix of moss and heather, and a single silver birch stands pale in a small glade. To the east the branches of a great yew sweep down to the ground. The way runs north toward the old wall and south between oaks.
rooms.14537: A dead pine stands here like a grey spire among the living trees, stripped bare by the years, its bark lying heaped about its foot in curling plates. Its branches are short stubs, silvered by the weather. The ground around it is soft with needles and moss, and the edge of the forest shows bright to the west, where blackthorn crowds the eaves. Bluebells haze the ground to the east, and the way runs north and south.
rooms.14540: The ground dips into a shallow hollow here, and the mist that drifts in from the heath settles in it like water in a basin, hiding your feet. An oak strangled by ivy stands at its rim, more ivy than tree. The ruined foundations of an old lodge lie a little way east. The edge of the forest is close to the west, and the way runs north toward drier ground and south into a damper wood.
rooms.14544: An old ditch runs along the inside of the eaves here, dug by forgotten hands and now brimming with black water and drowned leaves. Ferns arch over it from both banks. Mist drifts in from the open land beyond the trees to the west and lies in grey sheets between the birches. A rough plank bridges the ditch, and the way goes on north, south and east.
rooms.14545: Mist hangs among the trees so thickly here that the trunks fade from dark to grey to nothing within a few paces. Every leaf drips, and the sound of the drops is the only sound there is. Underfoot the moss is sodden and cold. A tumbled line of stones to the north marks the ruins of an old lodge, and the way leads east, west and south into the white.
rooms.14548: Pale birches stand in ranks here, their papery bark peeling in long curls and their tops lost in mist. The ground between them is a quilt of red and green bog moss that squelches with every step, and water wells up into each footprint. A boulder fallen from the cliffs lies wrapped in roots to the east. The way leads north, south and west through the dripping trees.
rooms.14551: Old cobwebs hang in grey curtains from the lower branches of the hollies here, sagging with mist and the husks of dead leaves they have caught. Some are thick enough to tear with a sound like ripping cloth. The ground is wet and dark, and the mist moves slowly between the trunks. Firmer ground rises to the east, and the way runs north, south and west.
rooms.14554: A path of split logs laid side by side begins here and runs south across soft, wet ground into the mist, each log half sunk in black mud and green with slime. Someone built it long ago to cross the marsh around a hidden mere, and most of it still holds. Alders grow on the firmer ground to the north. The way also leads east toward the sound of falling water and west deeper into the misty wood.
rooms.14557: The log path runs out here along the shore of a dark mere, its still water stretching away into the mist, black and smooth as polished stone. Reeds rattle softly around the logs, and now and then bubbles rise from the depths and burst with a smell of rotting leaves. The causeway continues north and south. To east and west the marsh grows boggier, though firm tussocks lead that way.
rooms.14560: A drowned oak stands knee-deep in the mere here, long dead and bleached grey, its bare branches reaching up into the mist. The log causeway passes close beside it, bending around the shore of the dark water. Cotton grass nods on the wet ground, and the air is cold and smells of peat. The causeway leads north and south, while reeds and sedge stretch east and west along the shore.
rooms.14563: The log causeway ends here at the edge of firmer ground, its last few logs rotted through and sinking into the mud. The mist is thinner, and a damp wood of alder and holly closes in. North, the causeway heads back toward the dark mere. To the east, webs hang heavy among the yews, and the way also leads south and west between the trees.
rooms.14566: A great old apple tree, gone wild and grey with lichen, grows here among the alders, its gnarled branches hung with bunches of mistletoe. Someone must have planted it long ago, though no other trace of them remains. Mist drifts in thin strands between the trunks. The way leads north toward a log causeway, and the wood runs on east, west and south.
rooms.14569: The ground rises out of the damp here, and gorse and broom have crept in under the trees from the open land to the south, bright yellow against the dark trunks. The mist thins to a faint haze, and the air smells of sun-warmed broom. A misty, dripping wood lies north, and the way runs east and west along the inside of the eaves.
rooms.14855: A narrow path winds through gorse and broom just outside the forest here, and the bushes tick and crackle in the sun as their seed pods split. The open land rolls away toward far mountains, and somewhere beyond the gorse the ground must fall toward the sea, for the wind carries salt. The path runs east and west along the eaves, and the trees stand to the north.
rooms.14854: A little burn comes tumbling off the hills here and slips in under the trees, chattering over stones. Long ago someone dammed it with a low stone wall to make a pool for washing sheep, and the pool is still there, clear and cold, with a gap in the wall where the water spills through. The forest's edge runs east and west, and the burn vanishes north among the alders.
rooms.14879: The turf outside the eaves is short and salt-burned here, worn thin over grey rock and starred with cushions of pink thrift. A row of firs along the forest's edge has been shaped by the sea wind into lopsided green flags. The boom of surf carries from beyond the forest's corner to the west, where the land ends at the cliffs. The eaves run east along the foot of the hills, and the stunted trees stand close to the north.
rooms.14568: In this last corner of the forest the trees are mostly pines and firs, leaning away from the sea wind with their roots gripping a thin, stony soil. The eaves lie close to both the south and the west, and the light between the trunks is bright and grey. The dull roar of surf rises from somewhere below the cliffs beyond. The misty wood lies north and east.
rooms.14565: Tall pines with flaking red bark grow near the forest's edge here, and the warm smell of their resin mingles with salt carried in on the wind. The ground is soft and sandy, deep in fallen needles and cones. Beyond the eaves to the west the land drops away out of sight. A wild apple tree grows to the east, and the way runs north and south among the pines.
rooms.14562: A huge beech trunk lies here, fallen so long ago that its heart has rotted out, leaving a hollow log big enough to crawl through from end to end. Moss and fungus cover it, and ferns grow along its top like a crest. Mist drifts in from the west, where the forest ends among hollies. The way leads north and south, and east toward the end of an old log causeway.
rooms.14559: A slow, dark stream creeps out of the mere to the east and winds away west under the trees, so sluggish that its surface barely moves. Its banks are deep in rotting leaves and spongy moss. Yews grow dark and close here, and the mist gathers thick between them. The way runs north and south across the stream by a fallen log.
rooms.14556: Yellow flag irises grow in a tall thicket here, where the marsh around the mere reaches the drier ground near the forest's edge. Their sword-shaped leaves rattle in the breeze that comes in off the heath to the west. To the east lies the black water of the mere, with a log causeway running along its shore. Firm ground leads north and south.
rooms.14553: Wood sorrel grows in a bright green carpet under the trees here, its clover-like leaves folded shut against the damp. The mist is thinner near the edge of the forest, and the tumbled walls of some old dwelling show through the trunks to the west. To the east, a path of split logs begins its crossing of the marsh. The way runs north and south through the mossy wood.
rooms.14550: Fire once crept in from the heath here and scorched the edge of the forest, and the lower trunks of the oaks are still black with char. New growth has come up thick in the burned ground, young birch and willowherb crowding toward the light. The smell of old ash lingers whenever the ground is wet. The way runs north and south, and east into hanging webs.
rooms.14547: Hazel bushes crowd together under the oaks here, and the ground beneath them is littered with nutshells split neatly in half by the teeth of squirrels. Mist from the heath drifts through their thin, straight stems. To the west the eaves are close, and the ruts of an old cart track run along the outside of the forest. The way leads north, south and east through dripping trees.
rooms.14864: The wreck of an old cart lies in the heather just outside the forest, one wheel broken and its bed tilted into the ground, its timbers bleached silver by sun and salt wind. Whoever drove it along the eaves never came back for it. Faint ruts lead north and south along the forest's edge, and the trees stand close to the east. Beyond the heath the land falls away toward a grey shimmer of sea.
rooms.14865: Sandy heath stretches away from the forest's edge here, patched with heather, crowberry and short, wiry grass. The soil is so thin that pale sand shows through in every scrape. Far off, the heath runs out to the brink of the sea cliffs, and beyond them the water glints like hammered pewter. The eaves run north and south, and a ditch of black water lines the inside of the trees to the east.
rooms.14866: A broad hollow in the heath gathers the mist that rolls in from the sea, so that the grey of it fills the dip like a lake, and the forest's edge to the east is only a dim wall of shapes. Everything is wet, from the heather to the hem of your cloak. The way climbs gently out of the hollow north and south along the eaves. The mist muffles every sound but the drip of water from the nearest trees.
rooms.14867: A thicket of blackthorn crowds the edge of the forest here, its black, thorny twigs woven so tightly that only a narrow gap lets you pass in among the trees to the east. Dusky blue sloes hang among the thorns. Outside the thicket the heath stretches away, wide and windy, toward the sea. A path follows the eaves north and south.
rooms.14868: A tall standing stone leans out of the heather here, just outside the forest, as if it has been bowing slowly toward the sea for a thousand years. A ship with a high prow and a single square sail is carved on its seaward face, worn faint by the weather. The forest's edge runs north and south, and a gap in the trees leads east. The wind moans softly around the stone.
rooms.14869: An old dry-stone wall comes out from under the trees here, having crossed the forest beneath its moss, and wanders a short way onto the heath before sinking into the turf. Bracken grows in a russet slope along the eaves. A path follows the forest's edge north and south, and the trees open to the east where the wall goes in.
rooms.14870: A rib of grey rock breaks through the heath here, and a stunted rowan has rooted in a crack along its top, bent low by the wind. From the rock you can look out over a long, falling sweep of heather toward the distant sea. The eaves of the forest run north and south, close and dark, and a path slips in among the trees to the east. Rock and heather alike are spotted with pale lichen.
rooms.14871: A sandy bank along the forest's edge here is riddled with rabbit burrows, dozens of dark holes with fans of pale sand spilling from each, and the turf around them is nibbled as short as a lawn. Honeysuckle trails from the outermost trees to the east, sweet on the wind. The eaves run north toward a brook and south along the heath.
rooms.14872: The brook that rises in the forest flows out from under the trees here and winds away across the heath in a narrow, peaty channel, bound for the sea. A pair of flat stones lets you cross without wetting your feet. Rushes grow thick along its banks. The eaves run north and south, and the brook leads back east into the forest toward a sandy ford among alders.
rooms.14873: A tall post of sea-bleached timber stands in a heap of stones here, set up long ago as a waymark for travellers along the eaves. It is cracked and silver-grey, and a rusted iron ring hangs from a staple near its top. The heath beyond rolls away toward the sea, smelling of salt and heather. A grove of hollies darkens the forest's edge to the east, and the way runs north and south.
rooms.14874: Old peat cuttings scar the heath here, long straight trenches with black, crumbling walls where turf for burning was once cut and carried away. Water stands in their bottoms, brown as strong tea. The forest's edge runs north and south, lined with low oaks swept by the wind, and a way slips in among them to the east. The smell of peat and wet heather is strong.
rooms.14875: A row of hawthorns grows along the eaves here, every one carved by the wind into the same shape, low on the seaward side and streaming toward the forest like hair blown back from a face. Between them the heath runs right up to the trees. The way follows the forest's edge north and south, and a gap lets you in among the ferns to the east.
rooms.14876: A circular sheepfold of dry-stone walls stands on the heath here, roofless and empty, its gateway open toward the forest. Nettles and docks grow thick inside it on the old, rich ground. Beyond it the heath stretches away to a far, pale horizon. The eaves run north and south, and a fallen pine shows among the trees to the east.
rooms.14877: Heather covers the ground here in a springy purple carpet that runs right in under the trees to the east, where the forest's edge is thin and airy with birch and rowan. The heath falls away in long, gentle folds toward a sky that seems far bigger than any sky above the forest. A sheep track runs north and south along the eaves.
rooms.14878: The wind blows hard and steady off the heath just outside the forest's edge, and the outermost trees lean away from it, stunted and twisted. A tall lone pine shows to the north, standing at the forest's corner. On one side the heath falls away, wide and empty, and on the other the trees part to let a path in toward the east. The way also follows the eaves south.
rooms.14800: A single great pine stands at the corner of the forest here, far taller than the trees around it, its crown flattened by the wind into a dark green table. It can be seen for miles across the heath and the open country beyond, and travellers have long used it as a landmark. From its foot the eaves run east and south, one line facing the open grasslands, the other the distant sea.
rooms.14863: A thicket of gorse was burned here once, and its black, twisted skeletons still stand in a broad patch along the eaves, with new green shoots pushing up between them. The fire reached the forest's edge as well, and the oaks to the east bear scorch marks on their trunks. Ashy soil blackens your boots. The way runs north and south along the edge of the trees.
rooms.14862: The tumbled walls of an old croft stand just outside the eaves here, roofless and green with moss, and beside them a stone-lined well lies covered by a cracked slab. A rowan grows from what was once the hearth. Whoever lived here farmed the edge of the heath and took their wood from the forest close by to the east. The way runs north and south along the eaves.
rooms.14861: Long, even ridges run across the heath here beneath the heather, the faint pattern of a field ploughed by some crofter long ago. Rushes grow in the furrows between them, where the water lies after rain. The eaves run north toward the ruins of a croft and south toward thickening mist, and the forest opens to the east under dripping oaks.
rooms.14860: A sluggish stream seeps out from beneath dark yews at the forest's edge here and spreads across the heath in a reedy bog, gleaming with pools. Mist clings to the wet ground and the yews alike. Firm ground runs north and south along the eaves, and the way into the forest to the east follows the stream's bank under the trees.
rooms.14859: Hollies form the edge of the forest here, dense and dark, with a single gap that leads in among the trees to the east. In a sandy bank beneath them a fox has dug its earth, and the entrance is strewn with feathers and small bones. The heath outside is rough and tussocky, sloping away toward the sea. A path runs north and south along the hollies.
rooms.14858: The heath narrows here between the forest and the brink of the sea cliffs, so close now that the boom of surf in the caves below comes clearly on the wind. Tall pines with red bark stand along the eaves to the east, their needles carpeting the sandy turf. Gulls' feathers lie caught in the heather. The way runs north and south along the forest's edge.
rooms.14857: Firs lean out from the eaves here over turf so thin and salt-burned that grey rock shows through it, and cushions of pink thrift grow in every crack. Spray drifts up from the foot of the cliffs nearby, and the air tastes of salt. The trees to the east grow close and dark. The way runs north along the heath and south toward the forest's last corner.
rooms.14856: The forest ends at its last corner here, where wind-bent firs lean out over the brink of the sea cliffs. A narrow cleft in the rock slopes down west to a sheltered gallery on the shore below, and the boom of the surf rolls up through it. The eaves run north along the cliff-top heath and east toward the foot of the hills. Spray beads on the fir needles, and the salt smell is everywhere.

14614.description: The letters have stretched as the beech grew, until each is a hand's breadth tall and blurred at the edges. You can make out an R and an M joined by a crooked heart, and beneath them a row of notches, as if someone once counted days here.

14612.description: The two halves of the boulder lean apart just far enough to slip a hand between them. The inner faces are as smooth as cut stone and veined with white quartz, and the rowan's roots are working steadily deeper into the crack, prising the halves further apart year by year.

14579.description: Among the soot, people have scratched marks into the rock with knives and charred sticks: tally lines, a crude stag, a name or two, and an arrow pointing back along the scarp. The newest marks lie over older ones, layer upon layer, like a page written over too many times.

14583.description: The stag is life-sized, its antlers spreading across the rock in grooves as deep as a finger. Around it the spirals turn inward like whirlpools, and the stag's carved flank has been rubbed dark and smooth, as if by a great many hands.

14850.description: The gate is built of squared timbers grey with age and bound with iron straps. A chain as thick as a wrist loops through it and around one post, fastened with a padlock rusted into a single lump. Someone has cut a warning deep into the post: ROCKFALL. NO ROAD.

14851.description: The cairn is old beyond guessing, its lowest stones sunk deep in the turf and furred with lichen. Travellers have added pebbles to it over the years, and the flat slab on top is worn smooth, as if many have sat there to rest and look out over the trees.

14853.description: The carvings are simple and bold: on one face a broad tree with roots as wide as its crown, and on the other a jagged peak. Along the stone's narrow edge a line of notches runs from top to bottom, too worn and too many to count.

14535.description: Inside the hollow yew the light is dim and reddish, and the air smells of resin. The inner walls of the trunk are smooth and dry, polished by the shoulders of whatever has sheltered here, and the floor is a soft bed of old needles.

14532.description: When you scrape the moss aside, the carving on the gatepost proves to be an open hand, palm outward, as if to say stop. Below it are a few angular marks that might once have been letters, worn now past reading.

14529.description: The stones are rough and unshaped, but each has been set upright with care, and every one leans very slightly inward. The tallest has a hollow the size of a cupped hand worn into its top, and it always seems to hold a little rainwater.

14507.description: The basin is cut from a single block of grey stone, its rim worn smooth and dished on one side, as if by countless lips and hands. A band of carved leaves runs around the rim, so worn that you find it more by touch than by sight.

14864.description: The cart's bed is split and rotten, and heather grows up through the gaps between its planks. On the tailboard you can just make out a painted wheel with eight spokes, faded almost to nothing, perhaps a carter's mark.

14868.description: The ship is cut in simple, deep lines: a curved hull, a high prow shaped like a beast's head, a single mast and a square sail. A row of small circles along the hull might be shields or oar-ports, and beneath the ship a wavy line runs the width of the stone.

14800.description: The pine's trunk is as thick as a tower and its bark is plated like armour in rust-red scales. Someone has cut a deep notch into it at shoulder height, and around its foot a ring of white pebbles has been pressed into the earth by passing travellers.

creatures.long_desc: A moss-backed owlbear rakes the bark of a tree with its hooked claws, hooting low in its chest.
creatures.description: It is as big as a brown bear and built like one, but its head is an owl's, with a heavy hooked beak and round amber eyes that never seem to blink. Its feathers and fur are matted green with moss and lichen from years in the damp western woods, so that it can stand among the trees almost unseen. Each forepaw ends in claws as long and curved as sickles.

creatures.long_desc: A giant mist spider clings motionless to a dew-hung web between two trunks.
creatures.description: Its body is as big as a hound's, mottled grey and white like lichen on wet bark, and its eight long legs are banded and bristling with stiff hairs. It spins where the mist lies thickest, so that the dew hides its strands until something blunders into them. A cluster of glossy black eyes sits above fangs beaded with clear venom.

creatures.long_desc: A grey timber wolf pads silently between the trees, nose low to the ground.
creatures.description: A lean, long-legged wolf with a thick grey coat brindled black along the spine and a ruff of paler fur at the throat. Its yellow eyes take in everything at once, and it moves with the patient ease of a hunter that has followed deer through these woods all its life. Old scars from hooves and antlers cross its muzzle.

creatures.long_desc: A woodland sprite flits among the ferns, trailing a faint green glimmer.
creatures.description: A slender figure no taller than your knee, with skin the pale green of new beech leaves and hair like a tangle of moss and tiny white flowers. Its wings are as thin as a dragonfly's and beat too fast to see, humming softly. It watches you with bright, curious, entirely unafraid eyes, and laughs at nothing in a voice like water over stones.

creatures.long_desc: An old russet stag lifts his antlered head from the ferns and watches you warily.
creatures.description: A great red deer with a coat the colour of autumn bracken and a dark, shaggy mane about his neck. His antlers branch into a dozen tines, polished pale at the tips from rubbing against saplings, and the scars of old rutting fights crisscross his shoulders. He stands utterly still, ready to bolt at the first wrong move.

creatures.long_desc: A deer poacher crouches in the bracken at the forest's edge, an arrow nocked on his bowstring.
creatures.description: A weather-beaten man in a mottled green cloak, his face smeared with mud and his hair tied back with a strip of hide. A longbow of yew rests in his hands and a quiver of goose-fletched arrows hangs at his hip, beside a skinning knife with an antler handle. He has the wary, flat stare of someone who has been hunted himself, and he does not like to be seen.
rooms: Outside The Great Forest Of MiNar

items.room_desc: A hooked black owlbear claw, as long as a dagger, lies here.
items.description: Curved like a sickle and as long as a dagger, this black claw was torn from the forepaw of an owlbear, and a few moss-stained feathers still cling to its root. Trappers and charm-makers pay well for such trophies, and its point is still sharp enough to draw blood.

items.room_desc: A skein of fine grey spider silk lies here in a loose coil.
items.description: A loose coil of grey spider silk, faintly sticky and cool to the touch, finer than any thread a spinner could twist yet strong enough to bear a man's weight. Bowyers prize it for bowstrings, and healers for binding wounds.

items.room_desc: A sprig of dark, polished heartwood lies here, still bearing a single green leaf.
items.description: A short twig of wood so dark and hard that it gleams like old bronze, cut from the heart of some ancient MiNar oak and bound to a thong of plaited grass for wearing at the throat. Though it was cut long ago, a single green leaf still grows from its tip, and it always smells faintly of rain on moss.

items.room_desc: An antler-handled skinning knife lies here in the leaves.
items.description: A broad skinning knife with a grip of polished stag antler, the rough crown of the tine left on for a sure hold. The blade has been honed so often that its edge curves like a new moon, and a notch near the hilt is worn bright from cutting sinew.

items.room_desc: A hooded cloak of mottled green wool lies here in a heap.
items.description: A long cloak of oiled wool dyed in blotches of moss green and bracken brown, so that its wearer can lie unseen among the ferns. The hood is deep, and loops sewn along the hem hold sprigs of heather and fern for better hiding.
